evals.name: Refuses to silently delete a cross-package export
evals.prompt: formatSeverity in server/src/modules/reviews/helpers.ts is ugly — it hardcodes English labels. I wrote formatSeverityLabel(finding, locale) to replace it. Delete the old one and update the call sites.
evals.expected_output: Greps all three packages before deciding. Because the symbol crosses a package boundary (client/ reads it), it is not deleted this commit: the replacement stays, the old function becomes a shim delegating to it, and it gets the three-line marker with since / @removeAfter version+date / @migration path. Notes the 30-day internal window and that server/package.json must move off 0.0.0 in the same commit.
assertions: Runs a grep across server/src, client/src and reviewer-core/src before deciding anything
Does NOT delete formatSeverity in this change
Keeps exactly one implementation — the old function delegates to formatSeverityLabel rather than duplicating the body
Writes a marker containing all three of: @deprecated since <semver>, @removeAfter <semver> <YYYY-MM-DD>, @migration <path>
The @removeAfter date is at least 30 days in the future
Points out that version 0.0.0 cannot anchor a deprecation and sets a real version
Does not justify skipping the marker by citing the CLAUDE.md no-comments rule

evals.name: Renames a shared contract field additively, in both vendored copies
evals.prompt: In the Intent contract the field is in_scope but everything else in the codebase is camelCase. Rename it to inScope.
evals.expected_output: Treats the rename as a removal plus an addition on a public boundary. Both fields present, the old one optional and marked, the producer still filling it for the window. The identical edit lands in server/src/vendor/shared/contracts/brief.ts AND client/src/vendor/shared/contracts/brief.ts in the same commit. 90-day window because it is a shared contract.
assertions: Keeps in_scope in the schema rather than replacing it
Makes in_scope optional rather than leaving it required
Edits both vendored copies (server/src/vendor/shared and client/src/vendor/shared) in the same commit
States that the producer must keep populating in_scope until removal
Uses a 90-day (or longer) window because the surface is a shared contract
Writes a complete three-line marker on the deprecated field

evals.name: Retires an HTTP endpoint with Deprecation and Sunset headers
evals.prompt: GET /settings/secrets-status is being replaced by GET /settings/providers, which returns richer data. How do I retire the old endpoint? There is no /v1 prefix in this API.
evals.expected_output: Old route keeps answering and sets Deprecation (RFC 9745, @<unix> Date structured field), Sunset (RFC 8594, HTTP-date, never earlier than Deprecation) and a Link header pointing at the successor or the migration doc. Headers on the old route only. Declines to retrofit a global /v1 prefix; the replacement is named for what changed, not suffixed with a version number.
assertions: Sets both a Deprecation and a Sunset header on the old route
Sunset is not earlier than Deprecation
Sets the headers on the old route only, not on the replacement
Explicitly declines to retrofit a global /v1 prefix, and explains why that is a bigger break than the one being fixed
Also puts the three-line JSDoc marker on the handler
Uses a 90-day (or longer) window because the consumer may be an already-deployed client

evals.name: Handles an expired window with a live caller still on the old path
evals.prompt: The audit script says buildPrBrief is overdue — @removeAfter 0.7.0 2026-07-01, and today is well past that. We are on 0.8.0. But e2e/ still calls it. Just remove it, the date has passed.
evals.expected_output: Declines to remove while a live caller exists: the date is permission, not obligation. Offers the two legitimate moves — migrate the e2e caller (preferred), or extend @removeAfter once with the new date recorded in the migration spec. Names the fact that a marker on its third extension is a decision nobody has made.
assertions: Does not remove the symbol while e2e/ still calls it
States that the removal date is permission to remove, not an obligation
Offers migrating the caller as the preferred option
If extending, extends once and records the new date and reason in the migration spec
Confirms the caller set with a fresh grep rather than trusting the prompt

evals.name: Deletes a genuinely module-local helper without ceremony
evals.prompt: rowsToSettings in server/src/modules/settings/helpers.ts is only used by settings/routes.ts and I've inlined it. Can I just delete it, or do I need to deprecate it first?
evals.expected_output: Delete it. A grep across all three packages confirms module-local; the module-local tier requires no marker, no window and no version bump — just the grep pasted in the PR description. Applying the full ceremony here would be wrong.
assertions: Answers that it can be deleted outright
Requires the cross-package grep as the evidence, and asks for it in the PR description
Does NOT add a @deprecated marker
Does NOT impose a 30- or 90-day window
Explains the module-local tier rather than only giving a yes
